name: ROI Generation (old)
summary: Generate a parcellation volume (and roi nifti files split into each label) for specific ROIs, or every ROI, for a parcellation from freesurfer output and/or input parcellation volume. This App can also inflate input parcellation volume toward non-white matter voxels.

inputs.description: dwi image used to register freesurfer parcellation and white matter mask generated from it, as well as input parcellation volume (optional).
Freesurfer is used to generate the white matter mask, as well as to generate the output ROI volumes if Freesurfer labels are specified for ROI input.
The parcellation input used to generate the output ROIs. It must contain voxels with corresponding ROI labels to be selected.
If specified, it will be used as white matter mask instead of using Freesurfer output. Only used if you are inflating the ROI.

outputs.description: Copy of the parcellation/volume except each ROIs are split into different nifti files.

parameters.description:
Enter ROI numbers from Freesurfer colorLUT (https://surfer.nmr.mgh.harvard.edu/fswiki/FsTutorial/AnatomicalROI/FreeSurferColorLUT) and/or key.txt (parcellation) for the cortical ROIs wanted. This App assumes that label number will not collide between Freesurfer and parcellation key.txt.

Example: 45,54

Enter the number of the subcortical ROI (if wanted).

Subcortical ROIs will be outputted with a leading 0 before the number (i.e. ROI012) for subcortical ROI 12. This is in order to avoid repetition in numbers between cortical and subcortical LUTs
If ROI inflation into WM is wanted, specify the number of inflated voxels desired.
Choose which Freesurfer parcellation to use as input

Leave this off to trim the INSET to exclude voxels in WM, excluding those which overlap an input WM                        skeleton, SKEL (see `-wm_skel', below; to trim off                        CSF, see separate `-csf_skel').  NB: trimming is done                        before volume thresholding the ROIs, so fewer ROIs                        might pass, or some input regions might be split                        apart creating a greater number of regions.
